instruction: Add butterflies(G, nodes=None) to networkx's bipartite algorithms (networkx/algorithms/bipartite/cluster.py, available as networkx.algorithms.bipartite.butterflies). A butterfly is a complete bipartite subgraph K_{2,2}: a 4-cycle whose nodes alternate between the two sides of an undirected bipartite graph. It returns a dict from each node to the number of butterflies that node belongs to, so each butterfly counts once for each of its four nodes and sum(values) == 4 * the number of butterflies: complete_bipartite_graph(2, 2) gives {0: 1, 1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 1}, K_{3,3} has 9 butterflies (6 at every node), K_{4,4} 36 and K_{5,5} 100. Every node of G is a key, with 0 when it is in no butterfly (isolated nodes included). nodes= only restricts which keys are returned: counts are always computed on the whole graph, and nodes not in G are ignored, as networkx.triangles does. Directed graphs raise NetworkXNotImplemented. Disconnected bipartite graphs work (no AmbiguousSolution). robins_alexander_clustering keeps returning the same values. Add tests.
